why: // is the remainder, as in the original R3 and in remainder; in this R3 (Oldes) // is integer division.
round/to keeps money when the value is money, whatever the scale; R3 gives the type of the scale (a decimal here).
mold of a function writes the code that makes it, as Red does (owner's decision, 2026-11-08); R3 writes make function! [...].
mold/all of a function is #[function!]: nothing loads a function back, so the construction form only names the type.
function writes its locals as /local in the spec it molds, as Red does.
function adds no empty /local; it molds as the func it is, as Red does.

test:
[o: make object! [w: 'red p: 'a/b n: none b: [x y]] (mold o) = {make object! [
    w: 'red
    p: 'a/b
    n: none
    b: [x y]
]}]
why: mold of an object quotes paths as well as words (p: 'a/b), so make object! gives them back; R3 quotes words only, and writes none as _ (Oldes).

test: [o: make object! [w: 'red p: 'a/b] o2: do mold o all [o2/w = 'red o2/p = 'a/b]]
why: Same: R3 molds p: a/b, which does not load back to the same object.

test: [mk: func [n] [does [n]] a: mk 1 b: mk 2 all [(a) = 1 (b) = 2]]
why: Every function keeps the words of the call that made it (func is a closure in Trebol); in R3 only closure does. The UI handlers and the tutorial rely on it.
An error! has the fields type id message near where at; R3 has code type id arg1 arg2 arg3 near where, and builds the message from a catalogue.

test: [e: try [cause-error 'user 'out-of-stock ["No" 'chain "left"]] all [e/type = 'user e/id = 'out-of-stock e/message = "No chain left" e/where = 'cause-error]]
why: Same error fields; where is the one function the error came from, not the stack of calls R3 lists.
Same: where is one word and near the expression of the program, also for errors inside the library.
Same error fields: cause-error takes the message itself, as there is no catalogue of messages.

test: [o: make object! [t: 2] same? o bound? in o 't]
why: bound? is kept as an alias of context?; this R3 (Oldes) dropped bound?.
context? of a function's word gives the frame of that call as an object; R3 has no frame as a value.

test: [e: try [x: ada@shop.example x/name] e/message = "cannot pick name in an email!"]
why: Same error fields (message).
enbase takes the base with /base, 64 if not given, as Red and the original R3; this R3 (Oldes) requires the base as an argument.
Same: enbase/base.
Same: enbase/base.
Same: debase takes the base with /base, 64 if not given.
Same: debase without a base.
Same: debase/base.
to-json is not in R3 core; Trebol has JSON built in (load-json, to-json).
Same: to-json.
An integer to a whole power stays an exact integer, as in Red; R3 always gives a decimal.
Same: an integer power that does not fit 64 bits is an overflow error, like any integer arithmetic; R3 gives a decimal.
arctangent2 takes y and x, as Red; R3 takes a pair.
mod gives the remainder with the sign of the divisor (as modulo in R3 and mod in Red); this R3's mod gives -1 here.
Same: mod with the sign of the divisor.
mod of times is exact: R3 goes through decimals and gives -0:00:59.999999999 here.
modulo treats a remainder too small to tell from the divisor as zero; R3 gives 0.1 here.
// is the remainder (see the integer case).
shift goes right unless /left, as Red (owner's decision, 2026-11-09); R3 shifts left for a positive count.
Same: shift/left is Red's.
Same: shift right keeps the sign.
Same: shift/logical is Red's.
The operators << >> >>> are Red's; R3 has none.

test: [(parse "aa bb" [collect [some [keep copy w to [" " | end] opt " "]]]) = ["aa" "bb"]]
why: A repetition stops when a turn matches without moving on; R3 goes once more and keeps an empty string at the end.
A malformed rule is an error that says so; R3 gives false.

test: [b: [1 2] parse b [change only integer! [x] skip] b = [[x] 2]]
why: change only is Red's: the block goes in as one value; R3 has no change only.
find/match gives the series after the match, as R2 and Red; this R3 gives where it starts.
reword takes the longest key that matches ( before ); R3 takes the first and leaves the s.
reword with a function gives its value once; R3 repeats text after it.
pad is Red's; R3 has no pad.
to block! of a string loads it, as Red; R3 puts the string in a block.
